paper.title: EmbodiedSWE: Coding Agents for Long Horizon Dexterous Robotics
paper.central_claim: Coding agents solve long-horizon dexterous simulated robotics and transfer prior solutions across tasks/embodiments; verified programs can be diversified into scalable VLA supervision improving held-out variation performance and enabling sim-to-real.

evidence.quote: Together, our framework uses coding agents to solve complex robotics tasks and turn verified solutions into scalable supervision for robot policies.
evidence.support_explanation: Original combined solver/teacher claim; not an assertion of generalist deployment.

evidence.quote: Agents have access to full simulator states, generic rendering and inspection tools, and configurable controllers, including operational-space and inverse-kinematics control.
evidence.support_explanation: Teacher privilege and execution interface.

evidence.quote: Grading is performed entirely offline to prevent agents from modifying scene code or exploiting the reward mechanism.
evidence.support_explanation: Separated grading intention; audit still necessary.

evidence.quote: For each run, we use Opus 5 to audit whether it is a reward hack, and score it as 0 if it is.
evidence.support_explanation: Model-based hack audit not independent human calibration.

evidence.quote: Each tool run uses two RTX 4090s rather than one; the second hosts the parallel simulations of the parameter search and the sweep tool.
evidence.support_explanation: Tool bundle compute confound.

evidence.quote: Mean score 0.66 0.70 0.44 0.51 Success rate 50% 43% 18% 18%
evidence.support_explanation: Bundle improves partial-credit means but not full success.

evidence.quote: Both no-hint rows use the same from-scratch Franka runs on the six target tasks.
evidence.support_explanation: Cross-embodiment no-hint comparator changes robot; cannot isolate hint effect.

evidence.quote: The tool restores the simulator state and returns the record of every branch already attempted from that node, including the code, action descriptions, and induced state and scene differences.
evidence.support_explanation: Checkpoint persistence and later retrieval.

evidence.quote: A recorded success is accepted only if it passes an open-loop action replay check.
evidence.support_explanation: Action-only replay gate on generated data.
Matched 1000-demo OOD rubric-score gain; not 23.3% task success.

evidence.quote: Evaluation seeds are disjoint from those used for data generation and paired across policies within each experiment.
evidence.support_explanation: Held-out initial conditions, paired evaluation.

evidence.quote: Clearing organic objects Complete the placement of one organic object. Pen holding Insert one pen into the holder.
evidence.support_explanation: Relaxed student success not original multi-object task completion.

evidence.quote: Sim-trained 100% 80% 30% 20% Pretrained \pi_{0.5} -DROID 0% 0% 0% 0%
evidence.support_explanation: Cumulative stages over ten trials: 2/10 end-to-end versus 0/10.

evidence.quote: We select the 14,000-step checkpoint based on real-robot performance.
evidence.support_explanation: Robot domain used for model selection; not independent sim-to-real holdout.

evidence.quote: However, we have not yet run this pipeline end to end to study how much of the coding agent’s capability it can transfer to robot policies.
evidence.support_explanation: Synthetic construction through distillation not end-to-end validated.

evidence.quote: Each setting is trained with three random seeds.
evidence.support_explanation: Student replication; solver base/tool runs only one per task.

evidence.quote: External restrictions interrupted the project before held-out evaluation could be conducted.
evidence.support_explanation: RL appendix training gains not deployment generalization.

evidence.quote: Generated trajectories are retained only if they pass the task grader and an open-loop replay check.
evidence.support_explanation: Fixed verified corpus selection.

evidence.quote: The policy-learning experiments in Section 4.2 evaluate increasing dataset sizes assembled through this framework; they do not isolate the contribution of individual diversification levels.
evidence.support_explanation: Explicit component-attribution limit.

evidence.quote: We remove human-designed interfaces on long-horizon tasks and find that frontier coding agents (e.g., Claude Fable 5) already write working solutions from scratch against Isaac Sim.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap relative to CaP-X macros, skill libraries, MimicGen and scripted data; independent neighbor originals not fixed.

evidence.quote: Newly recorded trajectories count only if their source code is unchanged since recording; an edited cell therefore needs new successful recordings.
evidence.support_explanation: Code fingerprint protects persisted trajectory provenance.

evidence.quote: The proprioceptive state is 8-dimensional, consisting of the seven arm joint positions and gripper closedness.
evidence.support_explanation: Student camera/joint-only inputs versus privileged teacher.
Author-reported full-task solver successes and hack rates on 28 tasks.

evidence.quote: API spend (USD, first-party list prices) of each run that solved its task
evidence.support_explanation: Cost disclosed for solved runs; failed-run token/time tables available but total failed-inclusive USD not reconciled.

gap.author_gap: Existing interfaces/benchmarks and seed-demo synthesis constrain long-horizon contact-rich coverage and scalable robot demonstrations.
gap.checked_gap: Within fixed local paper, full-state program generation plus controlled downstream data comparison supports this practical bottleneck; not an exhaustive novelty claim.

gap.closest_adjacent: CaP-X for coding-agent evaluation; MimicGen/script-only domain-randomized demonstrations for synthesis. Only author account available.

gap.remaining_gap: Strong attribution of individual tools/filter; calibrated grader; held-out real transfer; generalist distillation and trained-agent RL generalization.

X.reason: Program, checkpoint, generation cells, replay and BC interfaces reconstructable with explicit privilege and finite budgets; grader model calibration and observability conditions incomplete.

measurement.reason: Closed-loop task results and action replay, ten real trials; uncalibrated VLM/hack audit, relaxed student criteria and six-vs-eight scaling table mismatch limit measurement integrity.

causality.reason: Equal demonstrations and script-only training isolate broad diversification recipe, but not levels/filter; tool gain compute-confounded and cross-robot baseline mismatched.

holdout.reason: OOD scenes and disjoint paired seeds support restricted simulation generalization; robot checkpoint selected on real performance, appendix RL has no holdout.

statistics.reason: Task-wise denominator and student three seeds reported; single solver/tool seed, real n=10, no confidence intervals for stage comparison and inconsistent student summary.
